skill.name: systematic-debugging
skill.description: Guides AI coding agents through root-cause debugging before they propose or apply fixes.
skill.summary: A disciplined workflow for investigating bugs, proving root causes, and fixing only after evidence supports the change.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown fences, TypeScript template literals, normal NODE_ENV checks, and benign local script mechanics. I found no prompt-injection override text, but one diagnostic example can expose environment or signing details if copied directly into logs.

remediation.issue: Diagnostic shell examples can expose environment values and signing metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Change examples to print boolean presence only, redact variable values, and warn users before listing keychains or signing identities in shared logs.

remediation.issue: The find-polluter helper runs npm tests from user-supplied file patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Document that the script is manual-use only and should run only inside trusted repositories with reviewed tests.

content.user_title: Debug Bugs with Root Cause Discipline
content.value_statement: Random fixes waste time and often create new failures. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through evidence-based debugging before changing code.
actual_capabilities: Defines four phases for root-cause investigation, pattern analysis, hypothesis testing, and implementation.
Provides checklists for reproducing failures and reading error output before proposing fixes.
Explains how to trace bad values backward through callers to find the original trigger.
Shows condition-based waiting patterns for replacing arbitrary sleeps in tests.
Includes defense-in-depth validation guidance for preventing repeated invalid data bugs.
Includes a shell helper for identifying tests that create unwanted files or state.
limitations: It does not automatically inspect code or run diagnostics by itself.
It depends on the agent or user to follow each phase before making changes.
Examples may need adaptation for non-TypeScript projects or non-npm test runners.
Diagnostic examples must be redacted before sharing logs that may contain secrets.

use_cases.title: Investigate a Production Bug
use_cases.description: Guide debugging from symptoms to root cause before changing service behavior.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Flaky Tests
use_cases.description: Replace timing guesses with waits tied to observable conditions and clear timeouts.

use_cases.title: Review Repeated Failed Fixes
use_cases.description: Stop patch stacking and decide whether the design or shared state model is wrong.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a New Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Use systematic debugging. Read the error, reproduce the issue, check recent changes, and report the root cause before proposing a fix.

prompt_templates.title: Stabilize a Flaky Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Find why this test is flaky. Replace timing guesses with condition-based waiting only after you identify the failing condition.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Deep Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace this failure backward through the call stack. Show each caller, the bad value passed, and the original trigger.

prompt_templates.title: Recover After Failed Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: We tried three fixes and each failed. Stop implementation, question the architecture, list evidence, and propose the next investigation step.

output_examples.input: A test sometimes fails after waiting 300 milliseconds.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the real async condition, suggests polling for that condition, and explains why a fixed delay is unreliable.

output_examples.input: A git operation runs in the wrong directory during tests.
output_examples.output: The response traces the empty directory value through callers and recommends validation at the source and boundary layers.

output_examples.input: Three attempted fixes created new failures.
output_examples.output: The response stops further patches, summarizes evidence, and asks whether the architecture or shared state model is wrong.

best_practices: Start by proving reproduction and reading full error output.
Test one hypothesis at a time and record the observed result.
Add focused diagnostics that redact secrets and remove them after verification.
anti_patterns: Applying quick fixes before identifying the root cause.
Changing multiple variables at once and then guessing which change worked.
Leaving diagnostic logs that expose environment values or signing details.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for bugs, test failures, build failures, performance issues, and unexpected behavior.

faq.question: Does it fix code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives a debugging process. The assistant still needs project context and permission to edit files.

faq.question: Can I use it during an incident?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports fast triage by finding evidence before changing behavior.

faq.question: Does it require tests?
faq.answer: It recommends a failing test or minimal reproduction before implementation when possible.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are there security cautions?
faq.answer: Yes. Some examples use shell commands and diagnostics. Redact secrets before copying output into logs or chats.
